IMAGING: ○ Anterior temporal lobe lesions are most specific finding
○ Anemia due to marrow suppression/hemolytic anemia
CLINICAL ISSUES: • CMV is most common congenital infection worldwide with
no vaccine, no safe/effective therapy, and no universal
screening program
○ Humans are only known host
○ Vertical transmission: Transplacental fetal infection
• Congenital CMV responsible for 10% of cerebral palsy
○ Brain injury only occurs with 1st-trimester infection
• Serial US, MR > 95% sensitivity for brain anomalies in
fetuses known to be infected
• Negative fetal neurosonography/MR → strong negative
predictive value for poor outcome
DIAGNOSTIC CHECKLIST: • Invoke CMV in fetuses with growth restriction, echogenic
bowel, effusions, or any cerebral anomaly
• Postnatal CT/MR proven more sensitive than US allowing

entries.name: Токсоплазмоз
entries.definition: • Toxoplasmosis (toxo) is T in TORCH infections • Transplacental infection with protozoan Toxoplasma gondii
ultrasound_findings: Monthly ultrasound when suspected or confirmed infection
Confirm fetal infection by амниocentesis or cord blood
sampling for viral polymerase chain reaction
follow_up: All positive screening tests in pregnancy should be
confirmed in toxoplasmosis reference lab
Overall risk of congenital infection without maternal
treatment = 20-50%
1st-trimester infection less likely to result in congenital
infection (10-15%) but more likely to be severe
Later infection with much higher congenital infection rate
(up to 60% in 3rd trimester) but generally less severe
Sequelae of congenital infection include blindness,
epilepsy, intellectual impairment
Most infected infants asymptomatic at birth; up to 90%
develop sequelae
references: Woodward PJ, et al. Diagnostic Imaging: Obstetrics. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2021.

TERMINOLOGY: • Toxoplasmosis (toxo) is T in TORCH infections
• Transplacental infection with protozoan Toxoplasma gondii
IMAGING: • Monthly ultrasound when suspected or confirmed infection
• Confirm fetal infection by amniocentesis or cord blood
sampling for viral polymerase chain reaction
PATHOLOGY: • 3 principal routes of infection in humans
○ Ingestion of oocytes from contaminated soil or water
CLINICAL ISSUES: • All positive screening tests in pregnancy should be
confirmed in toxoplasmosis reference lab
• Overall risk of congenital infection without maternal
treatment = 20-50%
• 1st-trimester infection less likely to result in congenital
infection (10-15%) but more likely to be severe
• Later infection with much higher congenital infection rate
(up to 60% in 3rd trimester) but generally less severe
• Sequelae of congenital infection include blindness,
epilepsy, intellectual impairment
○ Most infected infants asymptomatic at birth; up to 90%
develop sequelae
